comments.body:
MATERIAL FOR THE ADR, discovered by executing J7 [rebar:b4e3-1de0-3188-40a1] and driving the DC
assembly against a REAL Jira instance for the first time. This is the epic's most transferable lesson
and the ADR should record it, because it is a property of the SEAM, not of the DC adapter.

THE FINDING: the Backend port does not state what the core actually requires.

  * 'TicketTransport' declares SIX members: create_issue, get_issue, update_issue,
    transition_issue_by_name, add_label, search_issues.
  * The core reconciler calls FIFTEEN distinct methods on a transport.
  * TEN of them are declared on NO Protocol anywhere in _backend.py: delete_issue, get_comments,
    get_issue_by_rest, get_issue_links, get_parent_map, remove_label, set_entity_property,
    set_issue_property, set_reporter, validate_assignee_exists.
  * All ten are implemented for Cloud (across acli_rest.py, acli.py, acli_graph.py); none on DC.

CONSEQUENCE, measured not theorised: a DC writing reconcile pass crashes with
'JiraDataCenterTransport object has no attribute set_entity_property' (CI run 30604756524) — while
isinstance(backend, Backend) passes, the backend contract suite passes, and 1636 reconciler unit tests
pass. Filed as [rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5], fixed by J9 [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36].

WHY IT BELONGS IN AN ADR RATHER THAN A BUG REPORT: ADR 0035's 'proof-of-seam' argument is that the
backend-agnostic contract suite is what certifies a backend. This epic shows that argument holds only
as far as the port is COMPLETE. A contract suite can only test what the port declares, so an
under-declared port yields a certificate that means less than it reads as — and it fails in the most
expensive direction, silently, at runtime, on the second backend rather than the first. The GitHub
adapter (epic be74) will hit exactly this unless the ADR names it.

SUGGESTED ADR CONTENT: state that a port's declared surface must be derived from the core's actual
call sites and kept honest by a STRUCTURAL TEST (J9 adds one), not by authorial discipline; and that
'the contract suite certifies a backend' is conditional on that. Also worth recording that the defect
was invisible to every static and unit-level signal and was caught only by a live pass — which is the
evidence for keeping a live tier in the seam's verification story at all.

RELATED, also for the ADR's provenance section: the shared-jira decision this epic makes was found to
be only PARTLY implemented. RemoteRef.instance — the field the decision leans on to distinguish
deployments — is NEVER CONSTRUCTED in production code (src/ has only the dataclass definition and
docstrings; the sole constructions are two test helpers). Filed as [rebar:6a91-7429-e521-4a2e]. The
ADR should not assert deployments ARE distinguished by RemoteRef.instance as though it were built;
state it as the intended design with the gap named, or the next reader will rely on a field nothing
populates.

LOOP ITERATION 3 — prep for this ADR while J9's plan review is in flight (deliberately not starting a
second concurrent review: the brainstorm log records that concurrent reviews worsened the Anthropic
API failures, and a --status call once blocked ~10 min on the store lock).

MECHANICAL FACTS for whoever writes the ADR:
 * Next free ADR number is 0055 (highest present is 0054).
 * CAUTION — THREE files already share the number 0035:
     docs/adr/0035-rc2b-snapshot-horizon-safe-replay.md
     docs/adr/0035-code-review-two-lane-tier-tagged-impact.md
     docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md
   This story amends the THIRD one. Any 'see ADR 0035' reference written without the slug is
   ambiguous in this repo, so cite the filename, not just the number.
 * That file's structure is Context / Decision / lettered subsections — e.g. '(a) Jira-coupling
   inventory' — so the amendment should follow the same shape rather than inventing one.

SUBSTANCE ALREADY RECORDED on this ticket (see the earlier comment): the port-incompleteness finding
and the RemoteRef.instance gap. Both are now backed by more evidence than when I wrote that comment:

 * The port declares SIX TicketTransport members; the core reaches for TWENTY-ONE. TWELVE are absent
   from the DC transport, and the same twelve are declared on no Protocol at all. Measured by AST
   audit over every attribute access on a client/transport receiver.
 * The dominant failure mode is SILENT: 7 of the 12 are swallowed by 'except Exception' at every call
   site, 3 are mixed, 1 crashes, 1 is hasattr-guarded. So a DC deployment appears to converge while
   not syncing comments, links, parents, properties, or validating assignees.
 * ROOT CAUSE is now separately ticketed as [rebar:cc77-8120-bcc6-47e8]: the core passes the transport
   as an UNANNOTATED parameter, so mypy cannot enforce port completeness. Proven three ways —
   unannotated: no error; 'client: Any': no error; 'client: TicketTransport': mypy rejects the
   undeclared call. The ADR's claim that 'the contract suite certifies a backend' holds only as far as
   the port is complete AND typed.

The ADR should state that conditionality plainly, because epic be74 (GitHub Issues) inherits the same
seam and will hit the same wall otherwise.

LOOP ITERATION 12. J8 review round 2: BLOCK, down to ONE finding — and it is a CROSS-TICKET
inconsistency I could not easily have caught myself. J8 said the core reaches for FIFTEEN transport
members; J9's description says TWENTY-ONE. Both cannot be right.

RE-MEASURED rather than trusting either number or my memory:
    call-form-only AST pattern (the NARROW one): 15
    every attribute access on a client/transport receiver (CORRECT): 21
    absent from the DC transport: 12
    found ONLY by the wider pattern: create_issue, delete_issue_link, get_issue, set_parent,
                                     set_relationship, update_issue

So J8 carried the stale undercount from my first, too-narrow audit; J9's 21 is right. Fixed, and the
plan now explains WHY the two numbers differ — the reconciler routinely passes transport methods as
VALUES (e.g. _call_with_retry(client.delete_issue_link, link_id)), which a call-form-only scan misses
entirely. That explanation belongs in the ADR too: it is the reason an audit of this seam must match
attribute ACCESS, not invocation.

Worth noting what the gate did here: it cross-checked two tickets against each other. Neither ticket
is internally inconsistent — the error was only visible by comparing them, which is a class of defect
I had no cheap way to detect on my own.

comments.body:
COMPLETION-VERIFIER REMEDIATION — the one unmet criterion is now implemented, not argued around.

THE FINDING WAS CORRECT. The AC has two halves: (a) `docs/user-guide.md` documents selecting the DC
backend and installing the extra, and (b) THE DOCUMENTED COMMANDS HAVE BEEN EXECUTED AGAINST THE J5
HARNESS. Half (a) was satisfied (user-guide.md:325-371). Half (b) was NOT, and the verifier's reason
for saying so was exact: the `jira-dc-harness` CI job runs the smoke tests, and none of them executes
the commands the guide actually tells an operator to run. Nothing in the repo demonstrated the
documented path had ever been driven.

I did not re-word the criterion. Executing the documented commands is a day's-worth-of-operator-time
question — a setup guide is precisely the artifact where an untested instruction is expensive, because
the reader follows it literally, it fails, and they cannot tell whether the guide or their instance is
wrong.

WHAT LANDED — change 1115, `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_user_guide_commands.py`.

The config block is PARSED OUT of `docs/user-guide.md` at runtime rather than restated in the test.
That distinction is the whole value: a hand-copied duplicate of the documented TOML would keep passing
while the guide rotted around it, which is the exact failure this criterion exists to prevent. If
someone edits the documented block into something that no longer selects the DC backend, or renames a
config key, the test fails.

A CONFIG-SURFACE POINT I CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. rebar reads bare `[reconciler]` from a
standalone `rebar.toml` and `[tool.rebar.reconciler]` from a `pyproject.toml`
(`_config_sources.py:111-115`). The guide documents the `[tool.rebar.…]` spelling, and the existing
live module (`test_reconcile_pass.py`) writes the OTHER form into `rebar.toml`. So driving the guide
through that module's fixture would have proven the guide works by not using it. The new test writes a
`pyproject.toml` — the surface on which the documented spelling is the correct one. Verified the
substituted block parses and resolves to
`{'backend': 'jira-datacenter', 'base_url': ..., 'allow_insecure': True}` with
`project` under `[tool.rebar.jira]`.

Three substitutions are made into the documented block, and each is itself documented in the same
section, so this stays a test OF the guide: `base_url` (the guide's value is an illustrative
example.gov URL) -> the harness; `project` -> the scratch project; and `allow_insecure = true`, which
the guide documents as the supported answer for a non-https instance and explicitly scopes to "a
loopback test instance, not a production bridge". The harness is plain http, so following the guide
FOR THIS DEPLOYMENT means setting it.

WHAT IS ASSERTED, BEYOND "EXIT 0"
 * the dry-run emits a `no_write` envelope. A run that exited 0 without one did not complete a pass —
   and a guide that tells operators to "inspect before enabling live sync" and then WRITES would be
   actively dangerous, so the no-write property is asserted rather than assumed from the flag name.
 * `mutation_failures == 0`.
 * no traceback on stderr.
 * the documented extra REALLY EXISTS: the `pip install 'nava-rebar[jira-datacenter]'` command is
   matched out of the guide and checked against `pyproject.toml`'s distribution name and
   `[project.optional-dependencies]`. Deliberately harness-FREE — a typo'd extra name is a
   documentation defect discoverable from the repo alone, and making that check wait on a live
   instance would leave a cheap verification unmade. Confirmed today: `nava-rebar` matches
   `project.name`, and `jira-datacenter` is declared at pyproject.toml:168.
 * JIRA_PAT is ENV-ONLY. The guide presents this as a security property ("never a config key, so the
   credential cannot be checked into a repo by accident"). A documented security guarantee that
   nothing checks is the weakest kind of claim, so the test writes the PAT INTO the config file,
   removes it from the environment, and requires the pass to FAIL with an error naming the variable —
   proving both that the config value is not honoured and that there is no anonymous fallback (which
   would turn a missing credential into a silently empty pass).

STATUS OF THE EVIDENCE. Change 1115 is pushed and awaiting `LLM-Review +1` / `Verified +1`. The
criterion is satisfied when the `jira DC harness smoke` job runs this module green — that job is the
only place the documented commands CAN be executed, since the harness base image is linux/amd64 only
and this workstation is Apple Silicon (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md:54-73`). I will record
the job result here before closing, and I will read the JOB, not the overall run status.

GitHub Actions run **30660546548**, job **"jira DC harness smoke (real Jira Data Center, ephemeral)"**,

THE CRITERION'S EXECUTION HALF — MET.
`test_the_documented_config_and_dry_run_work_against_a_real_dc_instance` **PASSED**. It lifts the

The harness-free half of the criterion (`pip install 'nava-rebar[jira-datacenter]'` names a real

THE ONE FAILURE IN THAT RUN, AND WHY IT IS NOT AN OBJECTION TO CLOSING.
`test_the_documented_setup_refuses_to_read_the_pat_from_config` — also one of this story's tests —
failed. It did not fail because the documentation is wrong; it failed because it CAUGHT A REAL PRODUCT
DEFECT: with `JIRA_PAT` absent from the environment and present only in config, the reconciler fell

# J8 — ADR amending 0035: the Jira-family sub-seam, shared provenance, and the DC horizon

## Context / Problem

ADR 0035 §6 states that "the first real second backend is out of scope for this ADR and is tracked separately
by epic `be74-7832-03a8-48ac`" — the GitHub adapter. This epic lands a different second backend first, and it
introduces a structure ADR 0035 does not describe: a `jira_family` layer between the neutral core and a
concrete adapter, with two contracts (`RichTextCodec`, `UserIdentityModel`) parameterizing it. It also makes a
provenance decision — that the Jira family shares one `jira` creation channel and `jira-` id prefix, with
deployments distinguished by `RemoteRef.instance` — which is precisely the decision PR #120 would have made
silently by inheriting the hardcoded literal `validate_creation_channel("jira")` — today at
`apply_inbound_records.py:211`, not :163 as an earlier draft of this plan said. Story J9's identity
fix shifted it, and line 163 now holds an unrelated tag list-comprehension. CITE THE SYMBOL, not a
line number: this plan has already gone stale against this exact file once. And it adds rebar's first
third-party runtime dependency in the reconciler, confined to an extra.

Left unrecorded, each of these gets re-litigated the next time a Jira-like tracker appears.

## Approach

Write one ADR that amends 0035 rather than replacing it, recording: the `adapters/jira_family/` layer and why
the seam is now two levels for one vendor family; the two parameterizing contracts; the shared-`jira`
provenance decision and explicitly what it defers to epic `be74` (generalizing `jira_key`, the `jira-` prefix,
and the channel vocabulary when a genuinely different vendor lands); the `pycontribs/jira` dependency, why it is
extra-gated, and why the Cloud ACLI path was deliberately not migrated onto it; and the Docker harness as the
verification oracle given that DC trial licenses ended in March 2026 and no official DC OpenAPI spec exists.

The ADR states the **horizon** plainly: Data Center goes read-only on 28 March 2029 and receives no new
features today, so this is a deliberately time-boxed investment for existing self-hosted clients, and the
durable asset is the family seam rather than the DC adapter. That framing is what tells a future maintainer
whether to extend this code or retire it.

The ADR must ALSO record two findings this epic produced by execution, both already evidenced on this
ticket's comments — they are properties of the SEAM, not of the DC adapter, so epic `be74` (GitHub
Issues) inherits them:

* **The port did not state what the core requires.** `TicketTransport` declares SIX members while the
  core reaches for TWENTY-ONE distinct transport members (an earlier draft said fifteen — that was a
  call-form-only AST scan; counting EVERY attribute access on a `client`/`transport` receiver finds
  six more, because the reconciler routinely passes methods as values, e.g.
  `_call_with_retry(client.delete_issue_link, link_id)`); TWELVE were absent from the DC transport and
  declared on no Protocol at all. The consequence was measured, not theorised: a DC writing reconcile
  pass crashed (`set_entity_property`) while `isinstance(backend, Backend)`, the backend contract
  suite, and 1636 reconciler unit tests were all green. So ADR 0035's "the contract suite certifies a
  backend" holds ONLY as far as the port is complete — and, per [rebar:cc77-8120-bcc6-47e8], only as
  far as the transport parameters are TYPED, since an unannotated `client` makes the gap invisible to
  mypy. State that conditionality plainly. Tracked by [rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5] and
  [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36]; the exception half is [rebar:bb8c-8283-80c6-4052].
* **`RemoteRef.instance` is NOT built.** The ADR must NOT assert that deployments *are* distinguished
  by it as though that were existing reality. `RemoteRef` is never constructed in production code —
  `src/` holds only the frozen dataclass definition and docstrings; the only constructions in the repo
  are two test helpers. State it as the INTENDED design with the gap named and tracked
  ([rebar:6a91-7429-e521-4a2e]), or a future reader will build on a field nothing populates.

**Alternative rejected:** documenting only in `docs/architecture.md`. rebar's ADR set is where rejected
alternatives live; without them the fork-per-deployment and hand-rolled-client options get re-proposed.

## Scope

- `docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md` (new — 0055 is the next free number; 0054 is taken by
  `0054-data-driven-calibration-no-costly-llm-assessments.md`).
  **Numbering caution:** THREE existing files share the number 0035 —
  `0035-rc2b-snapshot-horizon-safe-replay.md`, `0035-code-review-two-lane-tier-tagged-impact.md`, and
  `0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`. This story amends the THIRD. Every reference must cite the
  FILENAME; a bare "ADR 0035" is ambiguous in this repo.
- `docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md` — a pointer noting the amendment and correcting §6's
  "first real second backend" statement.
- `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/user-guide.md` — the `reconciler.backend` choice and the DC extra.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerated for `JIRA_PAT`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/user-guide.md` states the DC least-privilege expectation: a dedicated service account whose PAT is
      scoped to only the reconciled projects (Browse Projects / Create Issues / Edit Issues / Add Comments /
      Link Issues), never an admin token — and documents `allow_insecure` as cleartext-only-if-you-must, the
      `ca_bundle` key for internal-CA certificates, and `resolved_statuses` for workflows that do not use the
      conventional Resolved/Done/Cancelled state names (epic AC13)
- [ ] the ADR exists, is `Accepted`, and records each rejected alternative (fork-per-deployment, hand-rolled
      stdlib client, generalizing the store vocabulary now, migrating Cloud onto pycontribs) with its reason
- [ ] ADR 0035 carries a pointer to the amendment, and **all THREE stale statements** are corrected —
      not just Decision item 6. The claim that the first real second backend is out of scope appears
      at `:111` (layout-diagram comment `<backend-x>/  # future second backend`), `:204-205` (prose),
      and `:236-237` (Decision item 6). All three are falsified because this epic landed Jira Data
      Center AHEAD of the GitHub adapter `be74` was reserved for; correcting only one leaves two
      readers misinformed
- [ ] the ADR records the OSS-comparison finding [rebar:558e-55ce-d9f1-4fa9]: the seam ARCHITECTURE
      converged with what mature Jira integrations do (a maintained client library rather than
      hand-rolled REST, PAT bearer auth, an ephemeral containerised instance as the oracle), and every
      gap found was instead in OPERATIONAL EDGES that only appear against a differently-configured
      instance — index lag, server-side pagination caps, admin-toggled rate limiting, screen
      configuration, project moves. State that pattern, because it tells the next backend author where
      to look
- [ ] the ADR states the March 2029 DC read-only date and what it implies for future investment in this adapter
- [ ] `docs/user-guide.md` documents selecting the DC backend and installing the extra, and the documented
      commands have been executed against the J5 harness
